fields.name: Certified Community Behavioral Health Clinic (CCBHC): Planning, Development, and Implementation Grant (SM-26-014)
fields.funder: SAMHSA (HHS) — Center for Mental Health Services
fields.program: CCBHC-PDI; Assistance Listing (CFDA) 93.696; Grants.gov opportunity id 360977; authorized by PHSA Sec. 520A and PAMA Sec. 223
fields.eligibility: Statutorily limited to: community-based behavioral health non-profit organizations; organizations that are (a) part of a local government behavioral health authority; (b) operated under authority of the Indian Health Service, an Indian tribe, or tribal organization; or (c) an Urban Indian Organization under Title V of the Indian Health Care Improvement Act. Must be enrolled as a Medicaid provider (Attachment 11) and serve >=200 unduplicated clients annually. For-profits NOT eligible to apply directly.
fields.portal: Grants.gov (electronic submission required, Workspace-compatible package PKG00293348; NOFO also references eRA ASSIST forms). Due 11:59 p.m. ET on deadline day.
fields.accounts_needed: SAM.gov active registration with UEI; Grants.gov account; eRA Commons registration (NOFO says register at least six weeks before the deadline)
fields.match_required: No — 'Cost sharing/match is not required for this program.'
fields.page_limit: Project Narrative 15 pages (exceeding = not reviewed); Project Abstract 1 page; Budget Narrative no limit; Attachment 4 project timeline max 2 pages (excluded from narrative limit)
fields.attachments: 16 numbered attachments in Other Attachments form, incl.: #1 Letters of commitment + Evidence of Experience and Credentials (required) + Statement of Certification (incl. affirmation of >=200 clients served prior year); #2 data collection instruments; #3 sample consent forms; #4 project timeline (<=2 pp); #11 Licensure Checklist + Medicaid enrollment proof (application not reviewed without it); #14 Contingency Management Plan (if implementing CM); #15 service sites; #16 letter from State/District/Territory Behavioral Health Authority affirming approval of application (waived for Tribal applicants). Plus SF-424, SF-424A, SF-424B, Project/Performance Site, Lobbying forms.
fields.scoring_map: 100-pt merit review: A Need (10 pts, +5 priority points if serving one of the 100 highest all-intents drug-overdose-death counties in Appendix C — prime MORE targeting list); B Implementation approach (35 pts, incl. staffing/workforce plan to deliver 9 required services); C Proposed EBP/EIP (5 pts, ~1 page) — applicant names the evidence-based practice, appropriateness, modifications, and fidelity plan: the natural slot to name MORE with its RCT evidence; D Organizational experience and staffing (25 pts); E Data collection/performance measurement (20 pts) — MORE outcome literature supports measurable objectives. Required Activity #14 mandates workforce training that educates providers on evidence-based non-pharmacological interventions incl. psychotherapy; Allowable Activity #3 = workforce development/continuing education; Allowable Activity #10 = 'Provide training for CCBHC staff or community partners.'
fields.heart: $94M/yr to stand up 94 new CCBHCs (up to $1M/yr each, up to 4 yrs) — for-profits can't apply, so the win is a MORE training line item + named-EBP insert kit to applicants (Criterion C 5 pts, B 35 pts), aimed at the 100 priority overdose counties where +5 points are on the table.
fields.notes: Grants.gov synopsis confirms: posted 6/17/2026, close 8/17/2026, archive 9/16/2026, $94,000,000 estimated funding, 94 awards, ceiling $1,000,000, cost sharing false, status 'posted'. NOFO: award is up to $1M per year, project period up to 4 years; expected award date 11/15/2026, start 11/30/2026; CCBHC certification criteria must be fully met within 12 months of award; >=200 unduplicated clients/yr required; ~100 applications expected per package data. Companion NOFOs same 8/17/2026 deadline: SM-26-015 (CCBHC Improvement & Advancement, existing clinics) and SM-26-016 (state CCBHC planning cooperative agreements) — same insert-kit campaign can cover all three. accessible_usd left null: no training line-item dollar figure is stated in any source (per no-invented-amounts rule); training is fundable under Allowable Activities #3/#10 within each grantee's $1M/yr budget across 94 grantees.

discrepancies: Award structure nuance: claim says '94 awards x $1M' — NOFO states 'Estimated Award Amount: Up to $1,000,000 per year per award' with 'Length of Project Period: Up to 4 Years', so $94M is the estimated (annual) total and a single grantee can receive up to ~$4M over the full project period; Grants.gov lists $1M as award ceiling with $0 floor.

Eligibility precision: claim's 'local gov' shorthand is narrower in the source — must be part of a local government *behavioral health authority* (not any local government); eligibility also includes Urban Indian Organizations under IHCIA Title V, which the claim's 'tribal' shorthand only partially covers. For-profit exclusion confirmed as claimed.
Claim omitted that eRA Commons registration is required in addition to SAM.gov/Grants.gov (NOFO: register at least six weeks before the deadline) — no conflict, but material for the play timeline.

fields.name: NIH, CDC and FDA Small Business Innovation Research Grant (Parent SBIR [R43/R44] Clinical Trial Optional) — PA-27-100
fields.funder: National Institutes of Health (with CDC and FDA participation), HHS
fields.program: SBIR Phase I (R43) / Phase II (R44) Parent Announcement
fields.eligibility: U.S. small business concern: organized for profit, place of business in the US, >50% directly owned and controlled by US citizens/permanent residents (or qualifying VC/hedge/PE-majority structure with VCOC certification), not more than 500 employees including affiliates. fields.name: Community-based Opioid Recovery Effort (CORE) Multi-Year Regional Grants — Fall 2026 cycle

fields.eligibility: Per Amended 2026 Grant Issuance Plan: (a) TX state agencies and political subdivisions, and (b) 'any entity that engages in business in Texas in accordance with Title 34, Section 16.205 of the Texas Administrative Code' that (1) has a physical address within the RHP region applied for OR (2) provides services within that RHP region. fields.accounts_needed: OGMS account (create at txcomptroller.my.site.com/opioid — Create Account). No SAM.gov/UEI or eRA Commons requirement stated. Practical prerequisite: demonstrate 'engages in business in Texas' per 34 TAC 16.205 (employees in TX or fixed place of business).
fields.match_required: Not stated — no match requirement appears in the 2026 Grant Issuance Plan or the 2025 LT-CORE one-pager; final answer comes with the Fall 2026 NOFA
fields.attachments: Not yet published — application forms/attachments are defined in each NOFA, which for Fall 2026 has not been posted as of 2026-08-04
fields.scoring_map: Fall 2026 NOFA rubric not yet published. Plan-level signals: council gives PREFERENCE to proposals that expand MOUD access and/or prioritize pregnant/postpartum women; eligible categories explicitly include Workforce Training and Development plus Treatment and Coordination of Care (MORE clinician-training fits both); projects must be council-approved evidence-based abatement strategies per 34 TAC 16.201 — MORE's RCT evidence (dropout reduction, pain+OUD outcomes) scores at the evidence-based-strategy criterion. 2025 CORE process was 'multi-stage review including independent peer review' with final awards by the OAFC.
fields.heart: Up to $75M of Texas opioid-settlement CORE regional grants (3-5 yr terms) with a Workforce Training and Development category and for-profit-direct eligibility — MORE clinician training is a textbook evidence-based abatement strategy, and pairing it with the council's MOUD/pregnant-postpartum preference strengthens any proposal.
fields.notes: Structure: $75M divided among 20 Regional Healthcare Partnership (RHP) regions per 34 TAC 16.202(e)(1)(A) percentages (2025 one-pager shows the split: RHP 3 = 17.5% largest, RHP 6 = 9.8%, RHP 9 = 9.6%, down to RHP 13 = 0.7%). One award per region; separate application per region; entities serving multiple regions may apply in each region served. Award ceiling = 50% of the region's allocation (accessible_usd of ~$1.875M is derived: 50% x average region share of $75M/20; the largest region, RHP 3 at 17.5%, implies a ceiling near $6.5M). Grant term 3-5 years. As of 2026-08-04 the grant-opp page states 'No grant opportunities are currently open' and to revisit for 2026 updates — sign up for the OAFC listserv and watch ESBD. Companion cycle: Spring 2026 targeted grant, Opioid Abatement within the Criminal Justice System, up to $25M, awards $250K-$2.5M, 2-5 yr terms, same broad eligibility (total 2026 plan up to $100M). Reference deadline pattern from prior round: 2025 LT-CORE NOFA deadline was Feb. 10, 2026, 2 p.m. CT, so expect Fall 2026 CORE to post a NOFA in fall with a firm clock-time deadline. Contact: oafc.nofa@cpa.texas.gov / oafc.public@cpa.texas.gov.

discrepancies: Claim 'For-profits eligible' holds but is conditional, not blanket: applicant must engage in business in Texas per 34 TAC 16.205 (TX employees or fixed place of business, demonstrable as a condition of award), must have a physical address in or provide services within the specific RHP region applied for, must not be an opioid-litigation defendant/released party, and further disqualifications will be listed in the NOFA.

Claim 'Opens fall 2026' is the plan of record but no exact open date or NOFA exists yet; as of 2026-08-04 the OAFC page states 'No grant opportunities are currently open' — open_date left null, cycle_watch set to 2026-09-01.

Refinement, not contradiction: Fall 2026 CORE is a regional program — $75M is split across 20 RHP regions by fixed percentages, with one application per region and an award ceiling of 50% of that region's funds, so the practical per-application ceiling is far below the $75M pool and varies by region (~$260K to ~$6.5M at the 50% cap).

fields.name: OneOhio Recovery Foundation Regional Grant Cycle 3 (anticipated; Cycle 2 facts verified)
fields.funder: OneOhio Recovery Foundation (distributes 55% of Ohio's opioid settlement funds)
fields.program: Regional Grant Cycle — opioid abatement funds awarded via 19 OneOhio Regions
fields.eligibility: For-profits explicitly eligible: RFP p.4/8 lists 'A private, for-profit organization offering services that meet the charitable purpose of the Foundation' alongside 501(c)(3)s and state/local government. Must be in good standing, in operation at least 2 years (Foundation may request last two years of 990/tax filings), and headquartered OR actively operating in Ohio; Foundation checks registration/good standing with Ohio Secretary of State and requires a valid active EIN. Grants-page FAQ: must be 'registered under their current EIN with the Ohio Secretary of State for two consecutive years' (case-by-case review available if unable to meet it). RFP p.8: out-of-state organizations may apply ONLY if partnering with an Ohio-based lead applicant; grants-page FAQ softens this to out-of-state orgs 'currently operating in Ohio and properly registered with the Ohio Secretary of State.' Grant activities must directly serve people with SUD (incl. co-occurring MH) or affected family members.
fields.portal: OneOhio Grant Portal, accessed via oneohiofoundation.com/grants (all Funding Inquiries and Technical Applications submitted electronically there)
fields.accounts_needed: OneOhio Grant Portal account; valid, verifiable, active EIN; Ohio Secretary of State registration in good standing (FAQ: 2 consecutive years under current EIN — start Ohio foreign-LLC registration NOW to run the clock). No SAM/UEI, eRA Commons, or Grants.gov involvement.
fields.match_required: No cost match/share stated anywhere in Cycle 2 RFP. Constraints instead: administrative costs capped at 10% of award (over = disqualified); 5% of award withheld until satisfactory final report; no supplanting; must exhaust other federal/state/local funding first; no federal/state indirect-cost formulas.
fields.page_limit: No page limits; Funding Inquiry has per-question word limits ('submissions exceeding the specified word limits will not be considered'); question set posted on grants page before window opens.
fields.attachments: Step 1 Funding Inquiry is form-based (question set published in advance). Step 2 Technical Application (2-week turnaround after invite): budget on Foundation's Excel budget template; attestation of required licenses/certifications/accreditations; last two years of 990 or other tax filings on request; vendor quotes/bids for any capital costs; MOU with partners strongly recommended for collaborative grants.
fields.scoring_map: Regional Scoring Rubric (RFP pp.17-19) has an explicit 'Evidence' item: 'Does the proposal make it clear that the approach they plan to use has some basis in existing evidence or proven practice?' — MORE's RCT base (JAMA IM, ~59% dropout reduction, ~3x CBT) answers this directly. Second gate: recommended inquiries may go to the OneOhio Expert Panel, which screens that proposals are 'evidence-based and consistent with the OneOhio MOU' — Approved Purposes are defined as 'evidence-based forward-looking strategies.' Cycle 2 also published an Evidence Guide. Fit lanes: 'Workforce Development: Efforts to strengthen Ohio's behavioral health workforce' was a named Cycle 2 priority in Regions 2 (Hamilton — workforce retention/continuing education/healthcare-sector training), 11, 15, and 18; Treatment priority in most regions covers clinician training that expands SUD treatment quality/access.
fields.heart: Ohio's opioid-settlement regional grants ($45.8M in Cycle 2) explicitly fund for-profit vendors, and MORE clinician training hits both the rubric's Evidence criterion and the named behavioral-health Workforce Development priority.
fields.notes: pool_usd is the verified Cycle 2 total ($45,780,885 = $40M Board-approved June 2025 + Cycle 1 carryforward); Cycle 3 pool not yet set. accessible_usd = $186,000, the Cycle 1 average two-year award as stated in the Cycle 2 RFP (min request $25,000; only Region 2/Hamilton set a max, $500,000). Cycle 2 status as of 2026-08-04: funding inquiry closed 2/11/2026, inquiries under review; two-step process (Funding Inquiry -> invited Technical Application); 24-month projects starting on fixed dates 7/6/2026, 10/5/2026, 1/4/2027, 4/5/2027. Max 2 inquiries per region, may apply in multiple regions with region-specific budgets. Cadence reality check: Cycle 1 RFP 3/4/2024 -> Cycle 2 RFP 12/10/2025 (~21 months), so Cycle 3 may land mid/late 2027 rather than Dec 2026; cycle_watch 2026-12-01 tests the earlier hypothesis, and watch Board news mid-2026 onward (Cycle 2 budget was Board-approved ~6 months before its RFP). Play for More Therapy: register as Ohio foreign LLC with Ohio SOS immediately (2-consecutive-year clock), or partner with an Ohio-based lead applicant (RFP's stated path for out-of-state orgs) — e.g., an Ohio treatment provider or ADAMHS-adjacent nonprofit buying MORE training as a workforce-development line item. Services reimbursable by health insurance are unallowable costs — training is not, which favors the training-vendor angle. Questions: apply@oneohiofoundation.com.

discrepancies: 'Roughly annual, RFP expected ~Dec 2026' is NOT stated by the Foundation anywhere — no Cycle 3 announcement, no cadence statement exists. Actual cadence evidence: Cycle 1 RFP 3/4/2024 -> Cycle 2 RFP 12/10/2025, a ~21-month gap, which points to a possible mid/late-2027 Cycle 3 rather than Dec 2026.

Eligibility claim is incomplete: beyond 2-year Ohio SOS registration, applicants must be headquartered or actively operating in Ohio, and the Cycle 2 RFP (p.8) says out-of-state organizations may apply ONLY if partnering with an Ohio-based lead applicant (the grants-page FAQ softens this to 'currently operating in Ohio and properly registered'); a pure direct play from out of state is not supported by the RFP text.

The 2-year requirement also has a case-by-case exception per the grants-page FAQ, and the RFP phrases it as 'in operation for at least two years' with SOS good-standing verification, not strictly '2+ years SOS registration'.
Cycle 2 exact total is $45,780,885 ($40M newly authorized June 2025 + Cycle 1 carryforward), matching the claimed ~$45.7M.
The 2/11/2026 close was the Step-1 Funding Inquiry deadline (5 p.m. ET) of a two-step process, not a full application deadline; Technical Applications were by invitation afterward.

Performance-measures item rewards MORE's dropout-reduction/effectiveness data as projected outcomes. Cooperative Partnership competitive criteria add: collaboration with an organization having 'an established record of success treating, preventing, or reducing opioid use disorder' (statutory priority), addressing specific gaps, removing access barriers for high-risk populations, serving high-incidence and economically disadvantaged communities, and larger monetary match.
fields.heart: Recurring VA opioid-settlement pass-through where every city/county holds an entitled allocation (+25% Gold Standard bonus) plus a competitive coop pool (FY2027 city/county recommendations totaled $50,960,562.65 incl. carryforward) - applications must attach evidence-based documentation and contractor scopes of work, so MORE's RCT base and More Therapy as the named training vendor score inside locality applications.
